doc.title: Warren Bernhardt interviewed by Monk Rowe, Bearsville, New York, January 3, 2012

title: Closing message to future viewers and thanks
summary: His message about time being all at once, and thanks to Rowe.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: One more question, we’ve got four minutes by the way. So people, hopefully this archive is going to last a long time and for history, for generations to come, is there anything you want to say to people that are way beyond, haven’t even come to the planet yet, may be watching this.

Well maybe they’ll be aware by then that time works both ways and I’d like to thank them for their contributions to what we’re learning here now. It’s coming not only from what we’ve experienced in the past. Time is kind of an illusion, a dimension maybe. I would say I like the phrase “all at once” to describe everything. Therefore we’re all here now and there never will be anything but now for anything. So great to see you all. I’ve respected the future. I don’t think Atlantis has happened yet.
Well on that note, lovely. Thank you very much and it’s been a real pleasure talking to you. And I have to say I’ve admired your career from Steely Dan and all your own work.

Yeah, I’m proud of my recordings in a funny kind of way. It’s almost like they’re my children. I don’t do a lot of them, but they’re genuine. I’ve enjoyed this too. I didn’t think I was going to enjoy it and it turned out that I have so thank you.
